title: Convergence of real-valued $L^p$ norms
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p\in[1,\infty]$, let $F_m:X\to\mathbb R$ be in $L^p(\mu)$ for every natural number $m$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb R$ be in $L^p(\mu)$. If the $L^p$ norm of $F_m-f$ tends to zero as $m\to\infty$, then the real-valued $L^p$ norms of $F_m$ converge to the real-valued $L^p$ norm of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ is equipped with a measurable space structure
The extended-valued $L^p$ norm of $F_m-f$ tends to zero
